The hooks proposal item is therefore only partially implemented.

The package contains dual layers: prompts/ and services/{exa,firecrawl,deep-research}/. There are no package tests. API keys for Exa, Firecrawl, OpenRouter, and Next Public Firecrawl are injected via environment variables. promptctl validate is available. Python and TypeScript loaders coexist. Inventory docs still reference stale paths such as packages/prompts and apps/disclosure-rag. The tool registry still mentions Xata. Development-time personas are used rather than product runtime agents.

Prompt schemas are incomplete, as the README admits. Python prompt files share the prompts directory with YAML registries. Bulk documentation in prompts/methodology conflicts with block-new-docs. NEXT_PUBLIC_FIRECRAWL_API_KEY is exposed in the environment. The dual package nesting causes confusion. The C Keep/Change/Drop per proposal item is beginning.

MCP Neon and Linear are dropped for this package. There are no database writes here. Prompts and services do not need Linear tickets as primary DX. Neon MCP is a repo-level concern.

Lane-router is changed. It needs scoping to specific lanes such as prompt-edit versus services-edit versus dead-persona-doc. A prompt-validate skill would be better here.

Dod-report is kept at the repository level. It is not a package-specific automation.

Block git stash is kept because this package is doc-heavy and tempting to stash. Block-new-docs is changed; blanket blocking hurts prompt and methodology edits. Protecting .env is kept for API keys. Lockfile protection is dropped at this leaf.

Dod-auditor is dropped. There is no UI to dogfood. Security-reviewer is kept for services to catch API key leaks. A prompt-contract auditor may replace dod-auditor.

Security-guidance and typescript-lsp are kept. Typescript-lsp covers services/. Security-guidance is kept lightly for client environment patterns. Markdown prompts do not need it.

SessionStart is changed. It should inject only prompts/README, registry.yaml, and a note about deleted agents. Full MANIFEST injection is dropped.

Compact re-inject is kept only if personas return. Package-scoped worktrees are dropped. Scoped prettier is kept for services/*.ts only.

The search for two better package-specific automations is beginning.

Two concrete automation ideas emerged. A PreToolUse or Stop hook could run `bun run prompts:validate` on any edit under `packages/ai/prompts/`. Alternatively, an agent-definition integrity check could detect orphaned `MANIFEST.md` and `registry.json` files, or a "prompt registry drift" skill could diff `registry.yaml` paths against disk.

Hook risks are now clearer. Blocking new docs under `packages/ai/prompts/**` would falsely flag legitimate prompt authoring. The stash block is safe. Lockfile protection at the package level is risky because `bun.lock` must update when dependencies change. Injecting 18 deleted agent paths during SessionStart wastes context and may confuse agents into recreating them.

Prettier hooks on mixed Python, markdown, and YAML files risk mangling YAML prompts. The next step is to verify whether the shared directory was intended for deletion, confirm if any adversary agents remain, and count markdown files to gauge document bulk.
